# syq 0.8.0

This release improves local, remote and network-filesystem copying, adds file
selection expressions and more metadata options, and reworks SSH authorization
for copies between servers.

## Highlights

- Faster fresh local copies, small-file updates, block reuse over slow links,
  and copies onto NFS, SMB and SSHFS. Removal and pruning use less CPU.
- Preserve hard links, ACLs, extended attributes, access times and macOS birth
  times. Write sparse files with `--sparse`.
- Select files with `--where`, decide which entries to update with `--copy-if`
  and `--if-exists`, and update existing files with `--in-place=update`.
- Copies between servers use one enrollment per account and approvals signed
  by your own SSH key. Laptop-approved uploads keep going if the laptop
  disconnects. `syq ssh` can ask a laptop or SSH provider for account access
  without forwarding your agent.
- Clearer approval waits, SSH fallback notices and copy failures. Receiving
  services follow executable updates when idle, and status explains delays.
- S3 copies make fewer requests, reuse stored content hashes, handle throttling
  and outages more reliably, and support more object metadata.

## Compatibility changes

Several command-line options and Python keywords changed. `--preserve` is now
`--copy-metadata`, `--only-new` is `--if-exists=keep`, `--tcp-plain` is
`--no-tcp-encryption`, and `--inplace` becomes `--in-place=new` or
`--in-place=update`. Receiver receipt options and Python receipt types are gone.

A symlink named as a copy source requires `--follow-src` to copy its target or
`--src-non-dir` to copy the link itself. Links inside copied directories still
copy as links. Unchanged files keep their metadata unless `--copy-metadata`
selects it, and `syq map` emits only `src` and `dst` unless `--include` asks
for more fields.

Copies between servers enroll again on first use and require an SSH key login
to a non-root destination account. Existing enrollments remain usable by older
syq versions. Helpers now live in `~/.local/lib/syq`, and HTTPS uses the
system's CA trust store. Destination host-key checks follow the coordinating
server's SSH configuration, treating `StrictHostKeyChecking ask` as
`accept-new`; use `yes` to refuse keys neither machine knows.

Automation uses schema 4, or schema 5 for stream mappings, with times under
`timings`. Update the Python SDK and executable together. The matching Python
package is published after the native release.

See the [0.8.0 changelog](https://github.com/greaber/syq/blob/v0.8.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete behavior changes, compatibility notes and fixes.
